To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the β-Thr residue of the β subunit is essential for all F0F1 catalytic activities, and that it is not involved in the proton-decoupling process, whereas the β-Glu residue of the β-subunit is essential for proton-coupling and is involved in the proton uncoupling process.

the β-subunits of the chromatophores of R. rubrum are not essential for assembly of the F0F1 enzyme but are required for all the membrane bound F0F1 catalytic activities and that the β-sub-unit Thr159 is essential for Mg2+ binding and the β- Glu184 for the catalytic activity of the F0 F1 ATP synthase.
the β-Thr 159 and β-Glu 184 of the Rh. rubrumF0 F1 ATP synthase are ligands for the coupled Mg2+- and decoupled Ca2-dependent activities, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the β-subunit ligands to Mg2+and Ca2+ and their role in the proton-translocating F0F1ATPase of R. rubrum.
understanding the role of the β subunit of the F0F1-ATP synthase in the mechanism of ATP hydrolysis and proton translocation.
the identification of the catalytic site of the F1 ATPase and the mechanism of coupling between F1catalysis and F0 proton-translocation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Glu184 of β is essential for the proton-coupled and Mg2+-dependent F1 ATPase activities of chromatophore F1, whereas Thr159 of β is required only for the Ca2+ activity of the decoupled F1 ATPase activity of chromatophoreF0F1.

the F0F1ATP synthase has two different catalytic sites, one for Mg2+and Mn2+ and one for Ca2+, which can be distinguished on the basis of the β-subunit ligands and which can be used to distinguish between the two catalytic mechanisms.
Glu184 of β subunit is essential for F0F1 function, and Thr159 is required for Mg2+-dependent ATP synthesis and ATP hydrolysis but not for the decoupled Ca2+ATPase activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the β-subunits are involved in the binding of the Mg2+ ion and the Glu-184 residue is involved in the catalytic mechanism of the F1-ATPSynthase.

the β-subunits of the chromatophores F0F1ATP synthase have two distinct catalytic centers, one involved in Mg- and Mn2+-dependent ATP synthesis, hydrolysis, and proton-coupled CaATP synthesis and the other in proton-decoupledCaATPase activity, and that both centers are located at the β-subunit surface and are formed by the β-Glu184 and β-Thr159 residues.

the β-subunits Thr159 and Glue184 are involved in the binding of Mg2+ and in the catalysis, respectively, but that the conformational state of the catalytic β-subunit is different when the enzyme is activated by Ca2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the β-subunits of both the mitochondrial F1 and the bacterial F0F1 are not only involved in ATP synthesis but also in the control of this activity.
the β subunit is a highly flexible structure that can undergo significant conformational changes upon ligand binding.

, although the crystal structure of F1-ATPsase has provided us with a wealth of information, the differences between the mitochondrial and bacterial ATPases are such that the former is not a reliable model to explain the mechanism of the latter.
